candidates.title: Avoid repeated history tuple copies for already-valid streaming reasoning counters
candidates.statement: A guarded usage-counter interface could avoid copying all generated IDs on each chunk when the existing incremental reasoning counter is valid. Current standard-output CPU headroom is too small to prioritize implementation.
candidates.mechanism: serving.py builds tuple(generated_token_ids[i]); actual ready adapter delegates to an existing O(1) counter that ignores history. False-ready adapter reparses full history, requiring retained fallback.
candidates.proposed_change: Only if reopened: expose an explicit valid incremental-count capability and use it in continuous usage; retain original history semantics and fallback for nonready and legacy parsers. No global empty-history or mutable-list substitution.

prior_comparison.difference: S01 addresses input tokenization; this is output usage bookkeeping. Narrow lexical recall is not proof of novelty.

cpu_check.scope: Actual AST-extracted source methods and call expression; mocked parser state, not full parser or HTTP runtime. Seven repeated passes over same synthetic trace, not independent requests.

evaluation_plan.reopen_if: Real frontend CPU backpressure or profiling implicates continuous-usage copying on substantially longer outputs, or a separately justified maintenance change makes the safe capability cheap.
